r.문화권·종교: Same people, speaking Korean · religious activity controlled by the state
r.경제 체제: State-planned economy · sanctions block nearly all official trade, heavy reliance on China
r.정치 구도: The Kim family has passed down power for three generations, and the Workers' Party of Korea leads the state and the military. The supreme leader serves as both general secretary of the party and president of the State Affairs Commission, holding all power. There are elections, but with one candidate per seat they are not a way to change the government. Policy signals come from party congresses, plenary meetings of the Central Committee and the supreme leader's speeches. It tightly restricts people's movement and access to information and has laws that impose heavy punishment for bringing in outside culture.

t.why: Having carried out several nuclear tests since 2006 and test-fired intercontinental ballistic missiles, it has become the biggest variable in Northeast Asian security. The UN Security Council has imposed layer upon layer of sanctions on its exports and finance, but it is known to earn foreign currency by stealing crypto assets through hacking. It depends on China for most of its trade, and after signing a mutual defense treaty with Russia in 2024 it sent troops and weapons to help Russia in the war in Ukraine. The UN panel of experts that monitored sanctions enforcement was shut down in 2024 by a Russian veto. The UN General Assembly adopts a resolution condemning its human rights record every year.
t.rel: China is its biggest backer and effectively its only major trading partner. In 2024 it signed a mutual defense treaty with Russia and expanded military cooperation, while it faces off with South Korea, the United States and Japan over its nuclear program.
t.korea: An adversary that has faced South Korea for more than 70 years since the 1953 armistice ended the fighting of the 1950 war, and a neighbor that speaks the same language. There were summits in 2000, 2007 and 2018 and exchanges such as the Kaesong Industrial Complex and Mount Kumgang tours, but all have stopped. In 2024 it designated the South a 'hostile state' and cut the roads and railways linking the two. Missile launches, trash balloons and hacking go straight into Korea's security and financial news. Separated families, abductees and North Korean defectors remain unresolved issues.
t.know: Pyongyang's 105-story Ryugyong Hotel began construction in 1987 and has yet to officially open.
etext: It has deposits of minerals such as coal, iron ore, magnesite, zinc and rare earths. It once earned foreign currency selling them to China, but 2017 UN Security Council sanctions blocked most of its exports of minerals, seafood and textiles.

Since the sanctions, sending workers abroad, stealing crypto assets through hacking and arms deals have been identified as sources of foreign currency. Recently, deals sending weapons and troops to Russia in return for food, energy and money have grown.

It is a planned economy in which the state decides production and distribution, but since rationing collapsed, markets called jangmadang have become the center of people's lives. The authorities alternate between clamping down on and loosening the markets.
